To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diapycnal fluxes of nutrients in the Florida Straights can be as large as those observed in the open ocean.

the diapycnal flux of nutrients into the euphotic layer of the Florida Straits is 1) much higher than in open ocean, 2) highest at the shore, and 3) declines rapidly offshore as a function of decreasing nutrient concentration gradient.
the Florida Straits are a source of nutrients to the Florida shelf, and the magnitude of this nutrient source is highly sensitive to the value of the diapycnal diffusivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the Florida Current on the distribution and fluxes of nutrients to the euphotics zone in the Florida Strait.
the role of diapycnally driven nutrient fluxes in the Florida Straights.
the impact of the Gulf Stream on the Florida Current and how this affects the Florida Straits as a whole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Florida Straits are a nutrient source for the Florida shelf.

the diapycnal flux of nutrient to the euphotics zone is much greater than that in open ocean, and the magnitude of the flux is dependent on the diffusivity and the magnitude of vertical gradient of nutrients.
the enhanced nutrient supply in the Florida Straights is due to the uplift of the nutrient-rich deep waters by geostrophic flow of warm, nutrient-poor waters of the Gulf Stream.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nutrient fluxes to euphotic zone are enhanced along the Florida coast, but decrease rapidly with distance offshore.
the enhanced upward flux of nutrient is caused by the shoaling of the mixed layer and increasing nutrient vertical gradients.
the enhanced diapycnal mixing in the Florida Straights is the result of the interaction of the Gulf Stream with the Florida continental shelf.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Florida Straits is a unique location where nutrient fluxes are high and can potentially fuel high rates of primary production.
the Florida Straits are not a nutrient source to the Florida Current, but rather, the Florida Straits serve as a conduit of nutrients from the Gulf of Mexico into the Florida Current.
the enhanced diapycnal fluxes of nutrients along the shore of the Florida Straits may be due to the shoaling of mixed layers and increased nutrient vertical gradients.
